ledger.x: After the Persian Wars: the Paeonian kingdom.
356: Paeonia becomes subject to Philip II.
c. 280: Lysimachus's hold ends (page silent); the Celts of Brennus overrun Paeonia c. 280-279, so the end is a bridge.
c. 280: the Celts overrun Paeonia. 'It is certain that Paeonia was overrun and held for a time by their chieftain Brennus.'

c. 278: the Celts leave and Leon restores the kingdom. Infobox 'Leon reestablishes Paeonia after the Celtic invasion: c. 278 BC'; text: Leon 'later reestablished the Paeonian kingdom'. (Reviewer eu-01-x, 2026-10-18: year corrected from the bridged -279, confidence 1 to 2.)
227: the end of the Paeonian kingdom.

wars.name: Philip II's Paeonian campaign
wars.outcome: Philip bribed the Paeonians in 359/8, campaigned 'deep into the north, into Paeonia itself' in 358, and Paeonia 'became subject to Philip' in 356.

wars.name: Dardanian and Antigonid conquest of Paeonia
wars.outcome: The Dardani under Longarus captured Bylazora in 230; Antigonus Doson conquered southern Paeonia in 227; Philip V took Bylazora in 217.

certainty.note: No page gives a frontier; the page says Paeonia was 'separated from Dardania by the mountains through which the Vardar river passes' and ancient authors placed it north of Lower Macedonia, west of the Thracian mountains.
